title: Connecticut Sun trade Aneesah Morrow to Toronto Tempo
content:
Editor’s note: This article is part of our WNBA Trade Deadline coverage, which follows the moves reshaping the league.

Aneesah Morrow has been traded to the Toronto Tempo, the Connecticut Sun announced on Friday afternoon. The Sun have acquired the rights to forward Maria Kliundikova and the Tempo’s 2028 second round pick.

In a corresponding move, the Tempo waived guard Tima Pouye to maintain a 12-player roster.

Morrow was drafted by the Connecticut Sun with the seventh overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. In her second WNBA season, she rotated between a starting role and coming off the bench. In 20 appearances, she has averaged 11.6 points, 8.9 rebounds and 1.7 assists for the Sun.

She started all three of her final appearances for the Sun, and finished with 21 points and seven rebounds in Thursday’s 94-88 loss to the Chicago Sky.

The Sun are a franchise in flux. The 2026 campaign will be the team’s last in Connecticut before the team is relocated to Houston, where they will be rebranded as the Houston Comets under ownership of Tilman Fertitta, who also owns the Houston Rockets.

Because of the Sun’s positional overlap and desire to build a winner heading into the new market, there was a large sense around the league that the front office would be active at the deadline in an effort to further the rebuilding process.

The Tempo have been actively pursuing a young frontcourt star to pair with their explosive guard group, which includes rookie Kiki Rice and All-Star Marina Mabrey. The Sun turned down an offer from the Tempo earlier this season that included a first-round pick in exchange for Aaliyah Edwards.

“We’re thrilled to welcome Aneesah to our organization,” Tempo general manager Monica Wright Rogers said in a statement. “She’s a relentless competitor who impacts the game in so many ways, particularly with her ability to rebound at a high level. We believe she’s one of the emerging front court talents in this league, and we’re excited to see her play in a Tempo uniform.”

The Tempo are in a five-game losing streak that began before the All-Star break. They are about to start a five-game road trip, beginning with a two-game series against the Golden State Valkyries on Sunday.

The trade will be officially completed in the next 48 hours pending a physical. Morrow is expected to meet the Tempo in San Francisco, according to the team.
